fichas.title: Evaluation of Historic Building Significance
fichas.summary: Historic buildings may be valued for artistic, technical or scientific, historical, and urban-planning significance. The page illustrates these criteria with examples including Florence Cathedral, a mine, Goethe’s garden house, and the town plan of Karlsruhe.
uses: Assessing the cultural and historic significance of buildings and town plans
Supporting the evaluation of historic building substance

fichas.title: Conservation and Restoration of Historic Monuments
fichas.summary: Care of historic monuments aims to preserve cultural assets and their original substance, while practical use may require compromise between conservation and alteration. The comparison of conservation and restoration describes different aims and methods: conservation retains the building’s surviving historic fabric and visible history, whereas restoration seeks to make a selected historical condition clear. Both approaches have consequences and should be considered for each individual case.
uses: Evaluating and managing changes to historic buildings
Informing decisions about conservation or restoration

fichas.title: Historic Monuments in the Ground
fichas.summary: Archaeological monuments protect evidence of human history in the ground, including sites that are not yet known. Where possible, sites should remain undisturbed as an archive for future investigation. If preservation is not possible, recovery and documentation through archaeological excavation are required, including for remains found during building work.
uses: Preserving sites for possible future investigation
Recovering and documenting remains when preservation is not possible
